title: US and Ukrainian delegations meet in Jeddah and agree on 30-day ceasefire proposal
body:
On 11 March 2025, delegations from the United States and Ukraine met in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia. Ukraine was represented by Andriy Yermak, head of the Presidential Office, Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha and Defense Minister Rustem Umerov. The United States was represented by Secretary of State Marco Rubio and National Security Advisor Mike Waltz. The talks followed the confrontation between Presidents Donald Trump and Volodymyr Zelensky in the Oval Office on 28 February.

Ukraine said it accepted a US proposal for an immediate 30-day ceasefire along the entire front line, which could be extended by mutual agreement. The ceasefire would apply only if Russia adhered to it equally. Kyiv had separately proposed a partial truce covering the air and the sea, together with confidence-building steps, chiefly the release of prisoners. Ukraine said firm security guarantees from the United States and other partners should be a key part of any ceasefire.

According to Zelensky, the United States agreed to resume intelligence sharing and defense assistance, both of which had been halted after the 28 February clash. The joint readout said Trump and Zelensky agreed to pursue a comprehensive deal on developing Ukraine's critical mineral resources as soon as possible.

Russia was not present. A source close to the Presidential Office said Moscow's stance on a partial ceasefire was unclear, and Moscow had repeatedly rejected freezing hostilities along the current front line. US envoy Steve Witkoff was expected to travel to Moscow to meet Vladimir Putin in the following days.
